text.p: Indian tobacco and hotels group ITC Ltd said on Monday that it looked forward to bright business prospects in coming years after reporting a 28 percent rise in net profit in the first half of 1996/97 (April-March).
"The strong performance and growth potential of ITC's businesses augur well for the years to come," ITC said in statement accompanying the results.
"With its investment and business strategies well in place, ITC looks ahead to a bright future."
Britain's B.A.T Industries Plc is the biggest single shareholder in ITC with a 31.7 percent stake.
ITC's net profit rose to a record 1.81 billion rupees in the first six months of 1996/97 from 1.41 billion in the same period in 1995/96.
The Calcutta-based company said trading margins increased to 31 percent from 26 percent.
Pre-tax profit rose to 2.92 billion rupees from 2.32 billion despite one-off charges of more than 500 million rupees due to past issues, it said.
ITC said it had taken a cautious approach in accounting for receivables from ITC Global Holdings Pte Ltd Singapore, an wholly owned subsidiary which is under judicial management.

ITC Global Holdings has an estimated liability to bankers of $44.5 million, it said. The book value of stocks and receivables of that company is approximately $39.8 million and currently under examination by the judicial manager, it said.
"As a matter of abundant caution, the Board of Directors of the company (ITC) has provided for 349.9 million rupees on account of receivables from ITC Global Holdings Pte Ltd," the statement said.
The eventual outcome and consequent write-offs, if any, will be subject to all necessary statutory approvals, it said.

ITC said deferred revenue expenditure of 222.7 million rupees relating to the sponsorship of the 1996 World Cup cricket, brought forward from the previous yar, had been fully charged during the first half of 1996/97.
ITC said it had bought the Mantralayam plant and other facilities of ITC Agrotech Ltd for a total of 1.16 billion rupees, including sales tax, stamp duty and other levies.
It said the plant and facilities had been given on a non-exclusive licence to ITC Agrotech for five years.
